summary.headline: Best Agrolife Q2 FY27 revenue fell 21% to Rs 407 crore, but EBITDA rose 30% to Rs 101 crore on a 25% margin as patented mix rose.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 407 crore against Rs 517 crore a year ago, with management blaming an uneven kharif monsoon, delayed sowing, lower acreage and cautious farmer spending. Profitability improved sharply: gross margin reached 45% versus 33%, EBITDA margin 25% versus 15%, and PAT Rs 57 crore versus Rs 39 crore. Management said the decline came mainly from generic products, which fell about 30%, while patented products rose about 20%, with patented share of portfolio moving to 60% in H1 from 50%. Management said FY26 was the bottom and that H2 should not be loss-making, supported by higher sales-return provisions.

financial_highlights.change: -11% YoY (transcript cites Rs 898 crore in one place and Rs 893 crore in another for H1 FY26)
vs Rs 170 crore, 33% a year ago
+17% YoY; margin vs 31% a year ago

financial_highlights.metric: Opex excl. finance cost and depreciation Q2 FY27
Opex excl. finance cost and depreciation H1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: Rs 132 crore (as cited by analyst), current tax provision Rs 33 crore

segments.name: Patented products
segments.commentary: Patented portfolio rose about 20% YoY and its share of the portfolio rose to 60% in H1 FY27 from 50% in H1 FY26. Ronfen is cited as a top-10 product in India; Midcotin (paddy fungicide-insecticide) and SECTOR (insecticide, launched September) were launched in the quarter.

segments.name: Generic products
segments.commentary: Generic sales fell about 30% YoY across Best Agrolife and Sudarshan brands as management deliberately exited generic lines. Management said most of the revenue decline came from generics.

segments.name: Institutional / B2B
segments.commentary: Analyst noted about Rs 88 crore of the Rs 117 crore revenue decline came from institutional sales versus about Rs 22 crore from B2C; management did not dispute the split. Two patented molecules were supplied to SWAL Corporation (UPL subsidiary), and products are also supplied to Adama.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: A 47 MT generic export shipment to Sudan was valued at about Rs 5 crore. Registrations were received in Nepal (Ronfen), Mexico (Lambda), and 13 CIB registrations in the quarter; a Brazil step-down subsidiary was incorporated.

guidance_outlook: Management said it is 'not changing revenue' targets but also said FY27 revenue will not be a very big number versus FY26's Rs 1,256 crore, and it did not give a numeric H2 revenue guidance.
Management expects EBITDA and profitability to keep rising in H2 in line with H1, and said H2 should not be loss-making.
Higher sales-return and gross-margin provisions were created for H2; if returns come in lower, margins will be released, and management expects Q3 FY27 profit to exceed Q3 FY26.
Management said the 10-15% annual revenue growth target mentioned earlier is hard to say it can be achieved; it hopes for it by year-end.
Management said the CAPEX plan remains deferred until profitability is under control.
capex_capacity: CAPEX plan remains deferred; management will consider the next CAPEX plan only after profitability is controlled over the year.

One manufacturing plant is producing a specialised product (18-step backward synthesis) that is taking longer; unsold inventory from the previous and current season is expected to clear by March, with inventory reduction from February-March.
Management said specialised products have started at the plant this year and should support profitability.
demand_pricing: Kharif demand hit by uneven monsoon, delayed planting, lower planted area, soil moisture shortage and water-storage issues in Central, North and South India; cotton acreage fell in UP with cluster bean substitution.
Generic-category pricing pressure from competition was cited as a factor.

Sales returns: management said about 95% of sales returns had been received by end-October; a rule was set for sales teams to clear market inventory by early November. Higher provisions were booked for H2.
Rabi demand depends on crop growth, soil moisture, irrigation and farmer spending confidence; management said it is not appropriate to assume strong market recovery.
Fungicide demand was weak in UP due to low fungal disease pressure, while leaf folder in paddy supported spray products.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue fall so much when only about Rs 22 crore of the decline was B2C and about Rs 88 crore institutional?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the drop was driven by deliberate generic exits; patented share rose to 60% in H1 from 50%, and most of the reduction came from generics.

qa_highlights.question: Are the sales-return surprises from last year over, given the buffers now created?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY25-26 were bottomed-out numbers; 95% of sales returns were received by end-October, higher provisions were booked, and no surprises are expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the tax-case (Income Tax raid) matter closed, and what refunds are pending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 95% of cases from the 2023 raid are closed with no liability; about Rs 5 crore refund was received at Seedlings India and about Rs 15 crore is expected within a month.

qa_highlights.question: Why did long-term borrowings rise to Rs 73 crore from Rs 27 crore, and what is the cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 50 crore was drawn under a government-backed 20% additional working-capital facility, with a 1-year moratorium and 5-year tenor; cost of funds is 9.5-10%, and average cost is about 9.75-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise funds to strengthen the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an additional Rs 20-30 crore of working-capital debt may be taken; balance-sheet improvement is expected from inventory reduction from February-March rather than new equity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the September degrowth due to monsoon or market share loss, and how does it square with 10-15% growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed rainfall deficit, said it is not chasing revenue in the short term, and said 10-15% growth is hard to predict but it hopes for it by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sudan shipment and Nepal opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 47 MT Sudan shipment was an export of generics to an old customer worth about Rs 5 crore, with repeat discussions ongoing; Nepal interest is in patented products such as Ronfen.

risks_watch: Sales returns in Q3 and Q4; H2 margin depends on provision releases.
Rabi season demand and farmer spending, given uneven monsoon and water availability.
Inventory of specialised product at one plant (unsold this and last season) expected to clear by March; delay would keep working capital high.
Long-term borrowing up to Rs 73 crore and finance cost of about Rs 14-15 crore per quarter (consolidated); credit rating from CRISIL due in about a month.
Advance tax and interest exposure: management said the company pays advance tax mainly from January and some interest is expected on deferred payments.
Revenue growth targets (10-15%) are uncertain; FY27 revenue unlikely to match FY26 per management.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and patented-portfolio strategy but cautious on revenue; management repeatedly declined to give firm revenue or recovery forecasts and blamed monsoon and generic exits. Answers on the tax matter and borrowings were direct, but several answers were vague and some numbers were corrected mid-call (Sudan value, H1 revenue base).
key_quotes: So what we believe is H2, we should not be having losses.
So 95% of the sales return have been received. There could be some returns here and there but we do not expect any surprise going forward.
Our aim is exports. Our aim is international markets.

adds.what: Specialised product (18-step backward synthesis) started at one manufacturing plant this year; not a new capacity addition with stated size

growth.why: Management cut the 10-15% annual revenue growth target to doubtful, gave no numeric FY27 or H2 revenue guidance, and said FY27 revenue will not be large; H2 profitability is guided up vs H1 (not loss-making) backed by margin mix and sales-return provisions rather than new capacity, with CAPEX deferred.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin rose to 25% from 15% and H1 to 22% from 14%, with gross margin at 45% vs 33% as patented share hit 60%; management guides H2 profitability up in line with H1, though sales-return provisions cap upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management said the CAPEX plan remains deferred until profitability is controlled, and the only addition is a specialised 18-step product at one plant that is slow to clear inventory, not new capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue fell 21% YoY to Rs 407 crore in Q2 and H1 fell 11% to Rs 803 crore, with generics down about 30% from deliberate exits and management refusing to forecast a rabi recovery.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management explicitly said the CAPEX plan is still deferred and will be revisited only after profitability is under control over the year.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it is 'not changing revenue' targets but gave no numeric H2 revenue guidance and said FY27 revenue will not be large versus FY26's Rs 1,256 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The 10-15% annual growth target is now described as hard to achieve, and H2 margins depend on provision releases and on clearing inventory by March.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Midcotin and SECTOR were launched in the quarter and the specialised 18-step product started this year, with patented products up about 20% YoY and Ronfen a top-10 product in India.

rows.label: Inventory clearance by March
rows.why: Unsold specialised-product inventory from the last two seasons is expected to clear by March with reduction from February-March, but a delay would keep working capital and the Rs 73 crore of long-term borrowings high.

rows.label: Q3 FY27 profit above Q3 FY26
rows.why: Management expects Q3 FY27 profit to exceed Q3 FY26 as sales-return provisions are released if returns come in lower than provided.

rows.label: Export and registrations
rows.why: A 47 MT Sudan generic shipment (about Rs 5 crore), 13 CIB registrations, and Nepal and Mexico registrations were received, but the export scale is small against Rs 407 crore quarterly revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, the patented mix and the tax-case closure, but cautious on revenue and declined firm recovery forecasts; analysts pressed on the split between generic exits and monsoon-driven decline and on the rising borrowings.
